title: Week 2 Test — Fractions Operations & Algebra Basics
note: Drawn from Pixel's mapped week-2 lessons: volume, solving for x, variables, equations, plus fraction operations and cross-curricular practice.

questions.q: A box is 4 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 2 cm high. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.why: Volume = length × width × height = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cubic cm. Great job visualizing the unit cubes!

questions.q: If you fill a box with 36 unit cubes and the box is 3 cubes long and 4 cubes wide, how many layers high is it?
questions.why: Each layer has 3 × 4 = 12 cubes. 36 ÷ 12 = 3 layers. You're thinking in 3D!
Undo the +7 by subtracting 7 from both sides: x = 15 - 7 = 8. Nice inverse thinking!
Undo the multiplication by dividing both sides by 3: x = 21 ÷ 3 = 7. You've got the balance scale idea!

questions.q: In the expression 5 + n = 12, what does the letter n represent?
options: An unknown number we need to find
questions.why: A variable like n is a placeholder for a number we don't know yet. It's a math detective's clue!

questions.q: Which equation shows the rule: 'Multiply a number by 4, then add 3'?
questions.why: The rule says multiply first (4x), then add 3. That's exactly y = 4x + 3. You're reading math like a story!
Same denominator means same-sized pieces: 3 pieces + 2 pieces = 5 pieces out of 8. Smooth sailing!
Keep the denominator, subtract the numerators: 7 - 3 = 4, so 4/10. You're keeping the whole intact!
Split 20 into 5 equal groups (4 each), take 2 groups: 4 × 2 = 8. Fraction of a quantity mastered!

questions.q: In the sentence 'The curious robot explored Mars', what is the complete subject?
questions.why: The complete subject includes all the words telling who or what: 'The curious robot'. You spotted the whole team!

questions.q: Which of these is a sentence fragment?
options: The sun rises in the east.
questions.why: 'Because it was raining' leaves you waiting for the rest of the thought. It's a dependent clause, not a complete sentence. Sharp eye!

questions.q: When adding -ing to 'run', what spelling rule applies?
questions.why: Run has a short vowel + one consonant, so double the n: running. You've got the doubling rhythm down!

questions.q: Which property helps you identify a solid?
options: Takes the shape of its container
Has a definite shape and volume
questions.why: Solids keep their own shape and volume. That's why a rock stays a rock wherever you put it. Solid reasoning!

questions.q: Why did ancient cities often grow near rivers?
options: For water, farming, travel, and trade
questions.why: Rivers gave fresh water, fertile soil for crops, transportation, and trade routes — everything a city needs to thrive. You're thinking like a historian!
